relations.subject: n1ql:alter-vector-index

relations.subject: n1ql:alter-vector-index
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - promoted predicate. RECORDED WITH A CAVEAT: I assert this because the page states it in a direct quote, but it is almost certainly a content defect - see version_finding. relations.evidence: Altering indexes is only supported in Couchbase Server 5.5 and later; if any nodes in the cluster are running a version of Couchbase Server earlier than 5.5, then this statement will not work.

notable_absence.finding: Like createvectorindex.md, this page never states that the statement is new. Worse, it states the OPPOSITE: it claims 5.5-and-later and 6.5-and-later availability, inherited verbatim from alterindex.md. So for this statement availableSince is not merely absent, it is populated with values that must be wrong. Any pipeline that harvests availableSince from page text alone would confidently record that ALTER VECTOR INDEX has been available since Couchbase Server 5.5.

cross_component_finding: Same index-storage-technology gap as alterindex.json: the edition gate is phrased in terms of Standard GSI (Plasma), MOI and Forest DB, none of which have a home in the registry's storage-engine: namespace (couchstore, magma - Data service only). See alterindex.json.
cross_product_finding: Same divergence as alterindex.json, on a page that is a near-verbatim clone. Server 8.0: 'You cannot use this property if you have enabled file-based index rebalancing' (conditional on an opt-in setting). Capella: 'You cannot use this property in Couchbase Capella, as it defaults to file-based index rebalancing' and 'move You cannot use this action in Couchbase Capella, as it defaults to file-based index rebalancing' (unconditional, because of a platform default). The Capella record modelled this as `behavesDifferentlyUnder deployment:capella`; the Server page reveals the mechanism to be a setting, so the two can be unified as (deployment:capella defaults-to indexes:file-based-index-rebalancing) + (indexes:file-based-index-rebalancing disablesFeatureFor <clause>). Note the Capella record itself flagged that ALTER INDEX and ALTER VECTOR INDEX being documented synonyms means the coordinator may want to deduplicate rather than carry four independent findings - I agree, and the same applies across products: there are really two facts here (one Server, one Capella) presented across four pages.
version_finding: PROBABLE CONTENT DEFECT, and the sharpest version-vocabulary lesson in this batch. altervectorindex.md is a mechanical clone of alterindex.md - a diff of the two 8.0 pages shows only the statement name, the EBNF production, the syntax-diagram image, and the examples differ; every prose paragraph including all three version/edition gates is identical. That means this page asserts, of a statement that cannot predate 8.0 (vector indexes are introduced at 8.0 per createindex.md's own 'In Couchbase Server 8.0 and later' sentence): 'Altering indexes is only supported in Couchbase Server 5.5 and later', 'altering the number of replicas or deleting an index replica is only supported in Couchbase Server 6.5 and later', and 'This syntax provides compatibility with legacy versions of Couchbase Server.' All three are inherited boilerplate that is false or vacuous for ALTER VECTOR INDEX. There is a charitable reading - since ALTER VECTOR INDEX is a documented SYNONYM of ALTER INDEX, the 5.5/6.5 facts may be intended as facts about the underlying ALTER-INDEX capability rather than about the spelling - and if reconciliation accepts that reading, then isSynonymOf needs an explicit inference rule about which facts propagate across synonyms (version facts: no; privilege and edition facts: yes). Either way this page should be flagged as a docs issue: a new-in-8.0 statement page carrying pre-8.0 version gates. Relatedly, the whole vector-index family shows that availableSince cannot be harvested from statement-reference pages: createvectorindex.md omits it, altervectorindex.md contradicts it, and only createindex.md - which had to qualify a change to a pre-existing statement - states it correctly.
